To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 107-Gb/ s dual-mode dual-polarization OFDM signal is successfully transmitted over a 4-5 km two-mode fiber.
we have successfully demonstrated transmission of 107 Gb/s dual-mode, dual-polarization CO-OFDM signals over 4.5 km two-mode fiber.

we have demonstrated the successful transmission of 2.1 Tbit/s (2×107-Gb/s) dual-mode and dual polarization coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) over 4.5km two-mode fiber.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a novel optical mode multiplexer for mode division multiplexed transmission systems.
the development and implementation of a novel optical fiber transmission system for the transmission of 107-GBd CO-OFDM signals.
the design and analysis of optical fiber communication systems, and the experimental demonstration of high-speed transmission of mode-multiplexed CO- OFDM signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transmission of the spatial-mode multiplexing system with a mode-selective element is a viable and promising approach for future spatial multiplexing systems.
the results of the experiment demonstrate the successful transmission of a mode-multiplexed CO- OFDM signal over a mode-multiplexer and two-mode fiber.
the transmission of 107Gb/s dual-mode and polarization multiplexing (DM-PM) CO-OFDM over a 4km two-mode fiber is successfully demonstrated for the first time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 107-Gb-s CO-OFDM system with a 2.2-b/s/Hz spectral efficiency is demonstrated over a 4-km two-mode optical fiber.
the spatial mode dimension is a new and useful dimension in the design and implementation of high-capacity optical fiber communication systems.
the spatial-mode multiplexing is a viable technique to increase the transmission capacity in a cost-effective manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mode multiplexing and demultiplexing can be achieved with a low insertion loss and low polarization dependence loss.
the mode multiplexing and demultiplexing can be achieved with low insertion loss, low crosstalk and low complexity.
the mode-dependent chromatic dispersion can be compensated for by the digital signal processing (DSP) algorithm.
